messages:
amy_sales: kicking off a POC handoff for FathomHealth — they want a private deploy in their VPC, preserve client source IPs for logging/backoff, and route egress through their corporate TLS‑inspect proxy. Can we outline connectivity options, firewall rules they need, and an estimate of any extra monthly costs?
leo_neteng: TL;DR: PrivateLink (Interface endpoints) = easiest for network isolation, but you will NOT get original client src IP across the interface endpoint. PrivateLink terminates at our ENI and traffic will appear from those ENIs. If src IP preservation is required, VPC Peering / Transit GW path is needed (or a NAT44 solution in their VPC). :thinking:
sam_se: adding context — tradeoffs: PrivateLink = simpler routing + fewer route table changes, less ops for customer. Peering/TGW = preserves src IP but requires more routing config and may hit scale limits depending on number of accounts/spokes. Also call out TLS inspect: if they do MITM TLS inspect, that will break mutual TLS and client cert auth to our service unless they do cert passthrough.
gr ace_security: quick security checklist Qs: do they need PCI / HIPAA controls in addition to SOC? If yes, we'll need a Private deployment with customer KMS integration and audit logs forwarded to their SIEM. For firewall allowlist: initially we only need outbound 443 to our endpoints + DNS to their resolver.
ben_engineer: example SG / firewall snippet they can copy:

```
# egress rules (customer side)
- Allow TCP 443 -> our interface ENI CIDRs (we'll provide exact CIDRs per region)
- Allow TCP 1024-65535 -> our ENIs (for ephemeral source ports if using PrivateLink)
- Allow UDP 53 -> their DNS resolver or our resolver if using shared DNS
```

leo_neteng: note on IPs & NAT: if they need true client src for logging, two patterns:
- Pattern A: VPC Peering / TGW to our service VPC (preserves src).
- Pattern B: PrivateLink + preserve client IP by running a NAT/forwarder in their VPC that annotates original IP in X-Forwarded-For header (app-level). This requires app changes and is not transparent.
ben_engineer: also watch MTU for onprem tunnels / proxies — if they route via a corporate TLS inspect box which does encapsulation you can see MSS/fragmentation at ~1380. Recommend PMTU test early.
amy_sales: pricing question from customer — how much extra for PrivateLink vs Peering for POC? also any egress delta if traffic goes through their proxy vs directly to our hosted NLB?
ben_engineer: ballpark estimates for budgeting (POC scale, not final):
- PrivateLink: one-time setup + per-ENI cross-account connectivity overhead. Infra charge: ~"Connector PrivateLink add-on" (we'll scope on the quote). Network egress to our endpoints billed as normal egress; customer proxy path doesn't change our egress billing but may add their internal bandwidth charges.
- Peering/TGW: more engineering hours for routing & peering attachments; no PrivateLink add-on but potential TGW attachment fees on their side.
(we should follow up with Finance for an exact quote — these are not final prices).
infra_bot: deploy-bot: created ticket INF-1234: setup private endpoint CIDR allocation + generate ENI CIDR list for FathomHealth POC (assignee: ben_engineer).
leo_neteng: operational asks for POC kickoff call:
- customer VPC CIDR(s)
- desired AZs / region
- whether they can accept interface endpoints or require preserved src IP
- firewall admin contact + jump window for testing
amy_sales: next steps I propose: 1) schedule 30m handoff w/ neteng + sec + customer (this week), 2) ben to post ENI CIDRs & example SG by EOD tomorrow, 3) grace to attach security questionnaire answers (PII/PCI/HIPAA) before call.
sam_se: fine by me — I'll prep a 1-slide tradeoff matrix (PrivateLink vs Peering vs NAT) and a one‑para on TLS inspect impact.
gr ace_security: will attach short answers in the doc and list required KMS/audit items.
amy_sales: thanks all — tagging @fathom_contact to get CIDRs and proxy owner on calendar. :thumbsup:
